plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers in autumn without any leaves present. The strap-shaped leaves appear in spring and die back by summer, giving rise to its nickname 'naked ladies'.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Europe, naturalized in parts of North America; grows in damp meadows and woodland edges
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxic alkaloid that is used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce polyploidy.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, robust North American perennial wildflower topped with clusters of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It is a crucial late-season nectar source for pollinators and migrating monarch butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America in meadows, prairies, and roadsides
plants.funFact: New England Aster flower heads close up on cloudy days and at night, opening again with sunlight.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing subtropical tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often carpeting the ground beneath when the blossoms fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (September to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City' because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees that turn the streets purple each October.

plants.name: Osmanthus fragrans
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree bearing clusters of tiny, intensely fragrant flowers with a scent reminiscent of apricots and peaches. It is commonly planted in gardens and temple grounds across East Asia.
plants.location: Native to China and Japan; cultivated in warm temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Its blossoms are used in Chinese teas, pastries, and liqueurs, and are central to the Mid-Autumn Festival traditions in Guilin, a city whose name means 'forest of osmanthus'.
